entries.title: Study Skills Workshop Series
entries.content: The institute offers a free weekly Study Skills Workshop covering time management, active recall, and exam preparation techniques. Sessions run every Wednesday, 4-5 PM, in the Learning Commons. No registration required - drop in anytime.

entries.title: Peer Tutoring Program
entries.content: Students can book a free 1-on-1 peer tutoring session for any core subject through the Academic Support portal. Sessions are 45 minutes and can be booked up to 3 times per week. Tutors are senior students trained by the academic department.

entries.title: Structured Backlog Roadmap Template
entries.content: For students falling behind on coursework, a structured recovery roadmap breaks pending topics into weekly manageable chunks, prioritized by upcoming assessment weight and prerequisite dependencies, with built-in review checkpoints.

entries.title: Emergency Financial Aid Fund
entries.content: The institute's Emergency Financial Aid Fund provides need-based grants of up to a set amount per semester for students facing sudden financial hardship, including fee payment difficulty. Applications are reviewed within 5 working days by the Student Welfare Office. No repayment required.

entries.title: Merit and Need-Based Scholarship Matching
entries.content: Students facing financial stress can be matched to relevant scholarships based on academic standing, family income bracket, and program of study. The matching tool cross-references the institute's active scholarship database and flags eligible options with application deadlines.

entries.title: Student Counseling Center - Booking a Session
entries.content: The Student Counseling Center offers confidential 1-on-1 sessions with licensed campus psychologists. Students can self-refer or be referred through this system. First appointments are typically available within 3 working days. Sessions are free for enrolled students.

entries.title: Academic Probation Support Plan
entries.content: Students showing early signs of academic difficulty (grade decline, missed assessments) can opt into a structured support plan involving a dedicated academic advisor, biweekly check-ins, and adjusted workload pacing where institutionally permitted.

entries.title: Faculty Advisor Notification Protocol
entries.content: When a student's risk indicators persist despite Tier 1/2 support, their assigned faculty advisor is notified with a summary of the risk pattern (attendance, academic performance, or wellbeing signals) and invited to a brief check-in conversation with the student.

entries.title: Parent/Guardian Contact Protocol
entries.content: For students under 18 or those who have opted into family involvement, a parent/guardian contact on file is notified with a general wellbeing update and invited to a joint conversation with the academic advisor. This step always requires counsellor review before contact is made.

entries.title: Dean of Student Affairs Escalation
entries.content: PLACEHOLDER: For sustained, high-severity risk cases (score 40+), the Dean of Student Affairs office is notified for institutional-level review and coordinated response, which may include academic accommodations, welfare checks, or connecting the student with external support services.

entries.title: Campus Safety and Crisis Response Coordination
entries.content: PLACEHOLDER: In acute cases, the system flags the case for the campus safety/crisis response team, who coordinate with the counseling center and, where appropriate, external emergency services. This step always requires human counsellor sign-off before initiation - see guardrails module.
